title: VUA release.openForInspection (v0.2)
description: Tasked command face of the independent 'open in Unity to inspect/fix' entry (U19 user ruling 2026-09-21, BOARD row = normative source; v0.2 new method). The ruling keeps this path EXPLICITLY INDEPENDENT and OPEN regardless of the build record's state: opening the editor is neither recovery-execution nor upload permission, so a user may always open the project to inspect and fix it — including when the record's status would block a handoff (failed / cancelled / rolled_back / recovered), when the status is unconfirmable, and when the record has no status at all. Admission is the handoff admission MINUS the record-state gate: the params closed set {buildId} (a shape violation answers invalid_params), the wired faces (the unwired port answers unavailable — honest absence), the record existence (an unknown buildId answers build_unknown — the record is the authoritative project identity, ruling 4), and the editor-identity resolution (ruling 5: explicit injection > record's carried editor version among observed candidates > editor_unresolved). NO record-state classification happens on this route — never a whitelist pass, never a refusal. Completion judgment: the Bridge handshake arrival (001 chain), the same long-running task face as the handoff — 'process started' is never a completion judgment. The succeeded task snapshot's result carries the INSPECTION fact document, whose explicit operation key ('release.openForInspection') makes the wording un-mistakable: it is never a handoff completion fact and must never be presented as one (never '交接完成'). Like every face of this family there is no upload-status field — the upload happens in the official SDK and is never a VUA fact to guess at. Tasking: the unified task nine-state single form; the acceptance reply follows the tasked-command face.

buildId.description: The build-record identity anchoring the inspection (frozen build-record v0.3 face; the same identity family record.get serves). The closed params set: the build record is the single authoritative source for the project identity, so no project field repeats here.

errorCode.description: Closed four-code typed error set for the inspection entry. The record-state codes (record_state_blocked / record_state_unknown) are deliberately ABSENT: this route never classifies the record's status (the ruling keeps the inspect/fix path open regardless of state). unavailable: the route or the production-domain port is not wired — honest absence. invalid_params: params closed-set violations. build_unknown: the buildId has no corresponding build record (checked at acceptance time). editor_unresolved: editor identity failed to resolve; the diagnosis reuses the environment.verifyEditor semantics. Later-phase failures inside the running task (handshake timeout and the like) travel the ordinary task face nine states, not this set.

release-openForInspectionAccepted.description: Tasked-command acceptance (inspection.requestRun reply shape): poll the application task face by taskId; do not poll this method again. The succeeded task snapshot's result carries the inspection fact document.

release-openForInspectionFact.description: The inspection fact document (the succeeded task snapshot's result payload): the VUA-side terminal state of the editor-open-for-inspection. Six-key closed set: the handoff fact's five identity keys PLUS the explicit operation key — the wording discipline is pinned by shape, so this fact can never be read or presented as a handoff completion (the inspection entry is not a handoff; it grants neither recovery-execution nor upload permission). additionalProperties false also pins honesty rules 1/2: there is no upload-status field.

operation.description: The entry wording, pinned to the inspection operation. A fact carrying any other operation value is invalid by construction (the negative vector pins it).

buildId.description: The build-record identity the inspection anchored on.

projectId.description: Project identity resolved from the build record (authoritative identity face; never a filesystem path — storedPath discipline).

editor.description: The editor identity the inspection open targeted (identity facts only; exePath is the frozen editor-verify v0.1 fact family, not an artifact storage path).

exePath.description: The editor executable identity (editor-verify v0.1 fact family).

version.description: The editor version string (display form, as the verification face established it).

occurredAt.description: The instant the editor-open completed (RFC 3339), the VUA-side terminal-state fact.
